title: Report provenance record
description: The report.json written beside every published page. This is the source of truth for the report: the page is a rendering of it. Site-level figures are built from these records and never scraped from rendered HTML, which is what stops a claim that exists only in prose becoming a site-level number. Where the page and this record disagree, this record is what the run produced.

report_id.description: Becomes a public URL path and is permanent. Changing it breaks every link already sent. Certain names are reserved for generated source hub pages; publishing a report under one must be refused, because staging a report removes its destination directory first.

license.description: COMPUTED, never chosen. A report takes the most restrictive terms any contributing feed imposes, read from derivatives_license in the feed registry. Two different share-alike licences are refused rather than ranked, because that combination cannot be satisfied at all.

floors.description: Measured false-positive floors that licensed the claims on this page. A label with no measured floor at that site gets no card, however confident the model was.

runs.description: Run identifiers that produced this report.

review_status.description: 'model candidate' means a queue: model output published before anyone judged it. Nothing on such a page is an identification, and floors do not license it.

series.description: Position in a recurring series, where the report belongs to one.

review.description: Human review metadata, where a person has judged this page.

coverage_gaps.description: Known periods with no usable signal, stated rather than left to be inferred from a low count.

media_quality.description: How the bundled media was selected and what it is. Lets a reader tell a full source window from a trimmed clip.

model_refresh.description: Whether the model output behind this page is current or was inherited from an earlier run.

quality.description: The selection rule in force and the public claim it supports. Stating both is what lets a reader check that the claim does not exceed the rule.

redaction_allowances.description: Every redaction override used, recorded in the published artifact rather than only in somebody's shell history. An override takes a specific literal string, never a rule.

model.description: code_commit, license, lineage and caveat are nullable but should not stay null. A published claim whose model has no recorded commit cannot be reproduced, and one whose licence is unrecorded cannot be cleared.

floor.description: A false-positive rate measured for one label at one site. Floors are per site: pooling them lets a busy site clear a threshold on its own volume and then license claims at a quiet site that never earned one.

window.description: All three fields are nullable, and null carries meaning. A report whose coverage is naturally counted in something other than hours (video segments, frames analysed) records that count in 'counts' and leaves usable_hours null rather than fabricating an hours figure. What is NOT acceptable is a report that states no coverage anywhere: a day with no detections and a day with no recording look identical on a count, and coverage is the only thing that separates them.

usable_hours.description: Hours of USABLE signal, which is a stricter test than hours recording. READ from run artifacts, never typed: a hand-entered figure is a claim about provenance rather than provenance. Null where coverage is counted another way; see the note on this object.

counts.description: Deliberately open. The bundling counts below are common to every report; the rest are specific to what a given run measured, and inventing a fixed vocabulary for them would mean either lying or padding with zeros.

assets_missing.description: Must be 0 in a published report. Every local reference has to resolve inside the bundle, or publish refuses.

assets_dropped_for_budget.description: What did not fit the byte budget. Counted and reported on the page, never dropped silently.

source_paths_unparsable.description: Source paths that failed the lake path contract. Counted and reported rather than silently averaged in.

rightsRecord.description: Copied from the feed registry at publish time, so the report carries the rights position that was in force when it was built.

finding.description: One highlighted result. Two generations exist: earlier findings carry a prose 'evidence' field, later ones carry structured 'id', 'model', 'confidence' and 'timestamp'. Both are valid; new work should emit the structured form.

taxonomy.description: One label, or several where a finding sits under more than one.

confidence.description: The model score. SHOULD be a number. A string is accepted only because published data contains prose here ('Ecotype 1.00 Southern Resident, OrcaHello 0.97'), which is a defect: a consumer cannot compare, sort or threshold on it, and the number it describes is then recorded nowhere machine-readable. Emit a number and put the sentence in 'summary'.

path.description: Relative, content-addressed, and resolving inside the bundle. An image referenced from forty cards is copied once.
